---
title: "Summary"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

source("_common.R")

# Data flow rule: pages read_rds() only, never call an API. This page reads the
# frames the Inventory, Demographics, and Market pages already read, and quotes
# them -- every number below is computed, so the summary can't drift from the
# pages it summarizes.
stock <- read_rds("data/acs_stock.rds")
permits <- read_rds("data/bps_permits.rds")
demo <- read_rds("data/acs_demographics.rds")
pep <- read_rds("data/pep_migration.rds")
market <- read_rds("data/acs_market.rds")
burden <- read_rds("data/acs_burden.rds")
P <- read_rds("data/pums_profiles.rds") # written by r/pums/pums_profiles.R (core three, 2020-2024)

evict <- read_rds("data/evict.rds") # written by r/evict.R (court filings, core three)
hmda <- read_rds("data/hmda.rds") # written by r/hmda_prep.R (core three, principal residence, 1-4 unit)
audit <- read_rds("data/summary_audit.rds") # written by r/summary_audit.R: margins of error for quoted figures

first_yr <- min(demo$population$year)
latest_yr <- max(demo$population$year)
latest_bps <- max(permits$annual$year)

# formattable::comma()/percent() mask the scales versions (_common.R loads
# formattable after scales); inline text uses these thin wrappers.
n_fmt <- function(x) scales::label_comma()(x)
p_fmt <- function(x, accuracy = 0.1) scales::label_percent(accuracy = accuracy)(x)
d_fmt <- function(x) scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 1)(x)
pt_fmt <- function(x) sprintf("%+.1f points", x * 100)

# ---- Demographics ----------------------------------------------------------

pop_at <- function(g, yr = latest_yr) {
  demo$population |> filter(geoid == g, year == yr) |> pull(estimate)
}
pop_growth <- function(g) pop_at(g) / pop_at(g, first_yr) - 1

pep_eras <- levels(pep$era$era)
era1 <- pep_eras[1]
era2 <- pep_eras[2]
era_at <- function(g, e, col) pep$era |> filter(geoid == g, era == e) |> pull({{ col }})
per_year <- function(g, e, col) era_at(g, e, {{ col }}) / era_at(g, e, n_years)

intl <- pep$annual |> filter(geoid == "rr17", !is.na(international_mig))
intl_peak <- intl |> slice_max(international_mig, n = 1)
intl_last <- intl |> slice_max(year, n = 1)

n_natural_neg <- sum(pep$era$natural_change[pep$era$era == era2 & pep$era$geoid %in% unname(rr)] < 0)

age_share <- function(g, grp, yr = latest_yr) {
  demo$age_sex |> filter(geoid == g, year == yr, age_group == grp) |> pull(share) |> sum()
}
race_share <- function(g, grp, yr = latest_yr) {
  demo$race_ethnicity |> filter(geoid == g, year == yr, race == grp) |> pull(share)
}
hh_share <- function(g, grp, yr = latest_yr) {
  demo$household_type |> filter(geoid == g, year == yr, household_type == grp) |> pull(share)
}
inc <- function(g, yr, col = estimate_real) {
  demo$median_income |> filter(geoid == g, year == yr) |> pull({{ col }})
}
inc_real_growth <- function(g) inc(g, latest_yr) / inc(g, first_yr) - 1

under50 <- function(g, ten, yr = latest_yr) {
  demo$tenure_income |>
    filter(geoid == g, year == yr, tenure == ten, income_band %in% c("Under $25k", "$25k-$49k")) |>
    pull(share) |>
    sum()
}

# ---- Inventory -------------------------------------------------------------

units_at <- function(g, yr) stock$units |> filter(geoid == g, year == yr) |> pull(estimate)
units_growth <- function(g) units_at(g, latest_yr) / units_at(g, first_yr) - 1

vac <- function(g) {
  stock$occupancy |> filter(geoid == g, year == latest_yr, status == "Vacant") |> pull(vacancy_rate)
}
struct_share <- function(g, s) {
  stock$structure_type |> filter(geoid == g, year == latest_yr, structure == s) |> pull(share)
}
prewar <- function(g) {
  stock$year_built |> filter(geoid == g, year == latest_yr, era == "Pre-1950") |> pull(share)
}

reg_perm <- permits$annual |> filter(geoid == "rr17")
perm_peak <- reg_perm |> slice_max(total_units, n = 1)
perm_trough <- reg_perm |> slice_min(total_units, n = 1)
perm_last <- reg_perm |> filter(year == latest_bps)
recent4 <- reg_perm |> filter(year > latest_bps - 4)
n_mf_lead <- sum(recent4$multifamily > recent4$single_family)

# ---- Market ----------------------------------------------------------------

med <- function(frame, g, yr, col = estimate_real) {
  frame |> filter(geoid == g, year == yr) |> pull({{ col }})
}
real_chg <- function(frame, g) med(frame, g, latest_yr) / med(frame, g, first_yr) - 1

own_rate <- function(g, yr = latest_yr) {
  market$tenure |> filter(geoid == g, year == yr, tenure == "Owner") |> pull(ownership_rate)
}
hh <- function(g, ten, yr = latest_yr) {
  market$tenure |> filter(geoid == g, year == yr, tenure == ten) |> pull(estimate)
}

# Median value / median income, each window's own dollars (as on the Market page).
pti <- function(g, yr) {
  med(market$median_value, g, yr, estimate) / inc(g, yr, estimate)
}
rent_share <- function(g, yr) {
  med(market$median_rent, g, yr, estimate) * 12 / inc(g, yr, estimate)
}

b30 <- function(g, ten, yr = latest_yr) {
  burden |>
    filter(geoid == g, year == yr, tenure == ten, burden %in% c("Cost-burdened", "Severely cost-burdened")) |>
    pull(share) |>
    sum()
}
bsev <- function(g, ten, yr = latest_yr) {
  burden |> filter(geoid == g, year == yr, tenure == ten, burden == "Severely cost-burdened") |> pull(share)
}

# ---- Evictions and lending (core three) -------------------------------------

ev_sum <- function(g, col) evict$summary |> filter(geoid == g) |> pull(all_of(col))
ev_ann <- function(g, yr, col = "filings") {
  evict$annual |> filter(geoid == g, year == yr) |> pull(all_of(col))
}
ev_last_yr <- year(evict$last_month)
ev_pre_peak <- evict$annual |> filter(geoid == "bhc3", year < 2020) |> slice_max(filings, n = 1)
ev_trough <- evict$annual |> filter(geoid == "bhc3") |> slice_min(filings, n = 1)
ev_latest_full <- evict$annual |> filter(geoid == "bhc3", complete_year) |> pull(year) |> max()

hm_first <- min(hmda$rates$activity_year)
hm_last <- max(hmda$rates$activity_year)
hm <- function(g, yr, col, purp = "Home purchase") {
  hmda$rates |> filter(geoid == g, activity_year == yr, purpose == purp) |> pull(all_of(col))
}
hm_peak <- hmda$rates |> filter(geoid == "bhc3", purpose == "Home purchase") |> slice_max(originated, n = 1)
hm_low <- hmda$rates |>
  filter(geoid == "bhc3", purpose == "Home purchase", activity_year > hm_peak$activity_year) |>
  slice_min(originated, n = 1)
# Pooled denial rate by group over the last four years (same window as market.qmd).
hm_race <- function(grp, yrs = (hm_last - 3):hm_last) {
  hmda$by_race |>
    filter(race_ethnicity == grp, activity_year %in% yrs) |>
    summarise(rate = sum(denied) / sum(decided_apps)) |>
    pull(rate)
}
hm_reason <- function(r) hmda$reasons |> filter(reason == r) |> pull(share_of_denials)

# ---- Income bands (PUMS) ---------------------------------------------------
# The PUMS profiles cover the core three only, not the 17 localities -- see profiles.qmd.

ami5_lv <- P$levels$ami5
ami_b1 <- ami5_lv[1]
ami_b2 <- ami5_lv[2]
ami_b3 <- ami5_lv[3]
ami_b5 <- ami5_lv[5]

le80 <- function(ten, geo = "Core three") {
  P$le80 |> filter(unit == "Households", .data$geo == .env$geo, .data$tenure == .env$ten) |> pull(est)
}
pr <- function(tp, cat, band, ten) {
  P$profile |>
    filter(topic == tp, category == cat, .data$ami5 == .env$band, .data$tenure == .env$ten) |>
    pull(est)
}
pb30 <- function(band, ten) {
  pr("Cost burden", "Cost-burdened (30-49%)", band, ten) + pr("Cost burden", "Severely cost-burdened (50%+)", band, ten)
}
pbsev <- function(band, ten) pr("Cost burden", "Severely cost-burdened (50%+)", band, ten)

# Share of the region's 80%-of-AMI-or-less renter households living in Richmond city.
low_renter_city <- P$dist5 |>
  filter(unit == "Households", tenure == "Renter", measure == "count", geo != "Core three", band %in% ami5_lv[1:3]) |>
  summarise(n = sum(est), .by = geo) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n)) |>
  filter(geo == "Richmond city") |>
  pull(share)

# ---- External-affairs figures (BHC section) ---------------------------------
# Household counts by AMI band and tenure are PUMS (core three). Counts of
# subgroups (e.g. seniors) are band count x the group's share within that band.

hh_count <- function(bands, ten) {
  P$band_counts |>
    filter(unit == "Households", ami5 %in% bands, tenure == ten) |>
    pull(est) |>
    sum()
}
senior_hh <- function(bands, ten) {
  map_dbl(bands, \(b) hh_count(b, ten) * pr("Householder age", "65 and over", b, ten)) |> sum()
}
renters_le80 <- hh_count(ami5_lv[1:3], "Renter")
owners_le80 <- hh_count(ami5_lv[1:3], "Owner")
senior_renters_le50 <- senior_hh(ami5_lv[1:2], "Renter")
senior_owners_le50 <- senior_hh(ami5_lv[1:2], "Owner")
renters_le50 <- hh_count(ami5_lv[1:2], "Renter")
sr_share_le50 <- senior_renters_le50 / renters_le50
# Rounded for quoting: "about 41,000".
round_to <- function(x, k = 1000) n_fmt(round(x / k) * k)
# Margin-of-error text for a quoted figure, from r/summary_audit.R.
au <- function(key, col = "moe_text") audit |> filter(key == .env$key) |> pull(all_of(col))
```

The Richmond region's housing picture in one page: who is arriving, what exists, what it costs, and who carries the cost. Each section links to the page with the figures and tables behind it. Trends compare the ACS 5-year windows ending `r first_yr` and `r latest_yr` unless noted.

## At a glance

```{r}
#| label: tbl-glance

glance <- tribble(
  ~Indicator, ~Earlier, ~Latest, ~Page,
  "Population, 17-locality region",
    n_fmt(pop_at("rr17", first_yr)), n_fmt(pop_at("rr17")), "Demographics",
  "Population 65 and over",
    p_fmt(age_share("rr17", "65 and over", first_yr)), p_fmt(age_share("rr17", "65 and over")), "Demographics",
  "Median household income, Richmond MSA (real)",
    d_fmt(inc("40060", first_yr)), d_fmt(inc("40060", latest_yr)), "Demographics",
  "Housing units, core three localities",
    n_fmt(units_at("bhc3", first_yr)), n_fmt(units_at("bhc3", latest_yr)), "Inventory",
  "Permitted units per year, region",
    paste0(n_fmt(perm_trough$total_units), " (", perm_trough$year, " low)"),
    paste0(n_fmt(perm_last$total_units), " (", latest_bps, ")"), "Inventory",
  "Homeownership rate, region",
    p_fmt(own_rate("rr17", first_yr)), p_fmt(own_rate("rr17")), "Market",
  "Median home value, Richmond MSA (real)",
    d_fmt(med(market$median_value, "40060", first_yr)), d_fmt(med(market$median_value, "40060", latest_yr)), "Market",
  "Median gross rent, Richmond MSA (real)",
    d_fmt(med(market$median_rent, "40060", first_yr)), d_fmt(med(market$median_rent, "40060", latest_yr)), "Market",
  "Renters paying 30%+ of income, region",
    p_fmt(b30("rr17", "Renter", first_yr)), p_fmt(b30("rr17", "Renter")), "Market",
  "Owners paying 30%+ of income, region",
    p_fmt(b30("rr17", "Owner", first_yr)), p_fmt(b30("rr17", "Owner")), "Market"
)

glance |>
  rename(!!as.character(first_yr) := Earlier, !!as.character(latest_yr) := Latest) |>
  kbl(
    align = "lrrl",
    caption = paste0(
      "Headline indicators, ", first_yr, " and ", latest_yr, " ACS 5-year windows. ",
      "Dollar figures are in ", latest_yr, " dollars. Permits are Census Building Permits ",
      "Survey annual counts, not ACS."
    )
  ) |>
  kable_styling(c("condensed", "striped"))
```

## The region is growing, and migration is doing the work

- The region grew `r p_fmt(pop_growth("rr17"))` to `r n_fmt(pop_at("rr17"))` people, led by Chesterfield (`r p_fmt(pop_growth("51041"))`) and the four-locality expansion ring (`r p_fmt(pop_growth("secondary4"))`); Richmond city grew `r p_fmt(pop_growth("51760"))` and Henrico `r p_fmt(pop_growth("51087"))`.
- Natural increase fell from `r n_fmt(per_year("rr17", era1, natural_change))` people a year in `r era1` to `r n_fmt(per_year("rr17", era2, natural_change))` in `r era2`, so net migration now supplies `r p_fmt(era_at("rr17", era2, mig_share_of_growth), 1)` of growth. In `r n_natural_neg` of the 17 localities deaths exceeded births over `r era2`.
- International migration peaked at `r n_fmt(intl_peak$international_mig)` in `r intl_peak$year`; the latest year, `r intl_last$year`, was `r n_fmt(intl_last$international_mig)`.
- Richmond city flipped from domestic to international growth: its international migration rate rose from `r sprintf("%.1f", era_at("51760", era1, international_rate))` to `r sprintf("%.1f", era_at("51760", era2, international_rate))` per 1,000 a year while its domestic rate went from `r sprintf("%+.1f", era_at("51760", era1, domestic_rate))` to `r sprintf("%+.1f", era_at("51760", era2, domestic_rate))`.

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Full detail: [Demographics](demographics.qmd)
:::

## The population is older, more diverse, and more often living alone

- The 65-and-over share rose from `r p_fmt(age_share("rr17", "65 and over", first_yr))` to `r p_fmt(age_share("rr17", "65 and over"))` while the under-18 share fell from `r p_fmt(age_share("rr17", "Under 18", first_yr))` to `r p_fmt(age_share("rr17", "Under 18"))`. The expansion ring is oldest at `r p_fmt(age_share("secondary4", "65 and over"))`.
- The Hispanic or Latino share rose from `r p_fmt(race_share("rr17", "Hispanic or Latino", first_yr))` to `r p_fmt(race_share("rr17", "Hispanic or Latino"))`, and the White non-Hispanic share fell from `r p_fmt(race_share("rr17", "White non-Hispanic", first_yr))` to `r p_fmt(race_share("rr17", "White non-Hispanic"))`. Richmond city moved the other way: its White share rose from `r p_fmt(race_share("51760", "White non-Hispanic", first_yr))` to `r p_fmt(race_share("51760", "White non-Hispanic"))`.
- `r p_fmt(hh_share("51760", "Living alone"))` of Richmond city households are one person, against `r p_fmt(hh_share("secondary4", "Married-couple family"))` married-couple families in the expansion ring. Region-wide, `r p_fmt(hh_share("rr17", "Living alone"))` of households are one person.
- Real median household income in the Richmond MSA rose `r p_fmt(inc_real_growth("40060"))` to `r d_fmt(inc("40060", latest_yr))`. Renters are far behind: `r p_fmt(under50("rr17", "Renter"))` of renter households earn under $50,000, against `r p_fmt(under50("rr17", "Owner"))` of owners.

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Full detail: [Demographics](demographics.qmd)
:::

## The housing stock is single-family, older in the city, and built out in the suburbs

- The three core localities held `r n_fmt(units_at("bhc3", latest_yr))` housing units, up `r p_fmt(units_growth("bhc3"))`; the expansion ring grew `r p_fmt(units_growth("secondary4"))` from a much smaller base.
- Single-family detached homes are `r p_fmt(struct_share("bhc3", "Single-family detached"), 1)` of the core's stock and `r p_fmt(struct_share("secondary4", "Single-family detached"), 1)` of the ring's. Only Richmond city is substantially multifamily (`r p_fmt(struct_share("51760", "20+ units"), 1)` of units in buildings of 20 or more).
- `r p_fmt(prewar("51760"), 1)` of Richmond city's housing predates 1950, against `r p_fmt(prewar("51041"), 1)` in Chesterfield.
- Vacancy is tight in the suburbs (`r p_fmt(vac("51041"))` in Chesterfield, `r p_fmt(vac("bhc3"))` across the core) and highest in the southern localities (Sussex and Petersburg lead).
- Permitting bottomed at `r n_fmt(perm_trough$total_units)` units in `r perm_trough$year`, reached a series high of `r n_fmt(perm_peak$total_units)` in `r perm_peak$year`, and was `r n_fmt(perm_last$total_units)` in `r latest_bps`. Multifamily outnumbered single-family permits in `r n_mf_lead` of the last 4 years, and was `r p_fmt(perm_last$mf_share, 1)` of `r latest_bps` units.

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Full detail: [Inventory](inventory.qmd)
:::

## Prices rose faster than incomes; renters are no better off

- After inflation, the Richmond MSA's median home value rose `r p_fmt(real_chg(market$median_value, "40060"))` and median gross rent `r p_fmt(real_chg(market$median_rent, "40060"))`, against `r p_fmt(inc_real_growth("40060"))` for median household income (the rent and income changes are within each other's margins of error; the home-value change is not).
- The typical home was worth `r sprintf("%.1f", pti("40060", first_yr))` times the typical household income in the `r first_yr` window and `r sprintf("%.1f", pti("40060", latest_yr))` times in `r latest_yr`. Median rent equalled `r p_fmt(rent_share("40060", latest_yr))` of median income, from `r p_fmt(rent_share("40060", first_yr))`.
- Renter cost burden has not eased: `r p_fmt(b30("rr17", "Renter"))` of renter households pay 30% or more of income on housing (`r p_fmt(b30("rr17", "Renter", first_yr))` in `r first_yr`), and `r p_fmt(bsev("rr17", "Renter"))` pay half or more. Owner burden fell from `r p_fmt(b30("rr17", "Owner", first_yr))` to `r p_fmt(b30("rr17", "Owner"))`.
- Renter burden is now nearly identical across the core: `r p_fmt(b30("51760", "Renter"))` in Richmond city, `r p_fmt(b30("51087", "Renter"))` in Henrico, `r p_fmt(b30("51041", "Renter"))` in Chesterfield.
- Ownership held near two-thirds (`r p_fmt(own_rate("rr17"))`). Richmond city is the only core locality where renters outnumber owners (`r n_fmt(hh("51760", "Renter"))` renter households to `r n_fmt(hh("51760", "Owner"))`).

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Full detail: [Market](market.qmd)
:::

## Evictions have not fully rebounded, and lending has settled below its 2021 peak

- Eviction filings in the core three fell from `r n_fmt(ev_pre_peak$filings)` in `r ev_pre_peak$year` to `r n_fmt(ev_trough$filings)` in `r ev_trough$year` (`r p_fmt(1 - ev_trough$filings / ev_pre_peak$filings, 1)` lower), then recovered to `r n_fmt(ev_ann("bhc3", ev_latest_full))` in `r ev_latest_full`.
- The latest 12 months run at `r round(ev_sum("bhc3", "latest12_pct_hist"))`% of the historical average, `r p_fmt(-ev_sum("bhc3", "latest12_vs_pre"), 1)` below the 2016-19 monthly mean. Richmond city is furthest below baseline (`r round(ev_sum("51760", "latest12_pct_hist"))`%) and Chesterfield closest (`r round(ev_sum("51041", "latest12_pct_hist"))`%).
- Home-purchase loans originated for principal residences peaked at `r n_fmt(hm("bhc3", hm_peak$activity_year, "originated"))` in `r hm_peak$activity_year`, fell to `r n_fmt(hm("bhc3", hm_low$activity_year, "originated"))` in `r hm_low$activity_year`, and were `r n_fmt(hm("bhc3", hm_last, "originated"))` in `r hm_last`. Counting refinances, the swings are larger (`r n_fmt(hm("bhc3", 2021, "originated", "All purposes"))` in 2021, `r n_fmt(hm("bhc3", hm_last, "originated", "All purposes"))` in `r hm_last`).
- The home-purchase denial rate was `r p_fmt(hm("bhc3", hm_last, "denial_rate"))` in `r hm_last`, against `r p_fmt(hm("bhc3", hm_first, "denial_rate"))` in `r hm_first`. Over the last four years Black applicants were denied `r p_fmt(hm_race("Black"))` of the time and Hispanic or Latino applicants `r p_fmt(hm_race("Hispanic or Latino"))`, against `r p_fmt(hm_race("White, non-Hispanic"))` for non-Hispanic White applicants.
- Across all denied applications (all loan purposes, not only home purchase, `r min(hmda$reason_years)`-`r max(hmda$reason_years)`), debt-to-income (`r p_fmt(hm_reason("Debt-to-income ratio"))`) and credit history (`r p_fmt(hm_reason("Credit history"))`) are the most-cited denial reasons.

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Full detail: [Market](market.qmd). Eviction and lending figures cover Richmond city, Henrico, and Chesterfield only. Filings are landlord court requests, not completed evictions, and the 2020-21 trough reflects pandemic moratoria and rental assistance. Lending counts cover one- to four-unit principal residences.
:::

## Lower-income renters carry the cost burden, and most live in Henrico and Chesterfield

- `r p_fmt(le80("All households"))` of households in the core three earn 80% of area median income (AMI) or less: `r p_fmt(le80("Renter"))` of renters and `r p_fmt(le80("Owner"))` of owners.
- Richmond city has the highest share (`r p_fmt(le80("All households", "Richmond city"))`, against `r p_fmt(le80("All households", "Henrico County"))` in Henrico and `r p_fmt(le80("All households", "Chesterfield County"))` in Chesterfield), but only `r p_fmt(low_renter_city)` of the core three's lower-income renter households live in the city.
- `r p_fmt(pbsev(ami_b1, "Renter"))` of renters at 30% of AMI or less pay half or more of income on housing, and `r p_fmt(pb30(ami_b3, "Renter"))` of renters at 51-80% of AMI pay 30% or more; above 120% of AMI, about `r p_fmt(pb30(ami_b5, "Renter"), 1)` do (a small sample).
- The lowest-income renters are mostly people living alone (`r p_fmt(pr("Household type", "Living alone", ami_b1, "Renter"))`) and are `r p_fmt(pr("Householder race and ethnicity", "Black", ami_b1, "Renter"))` Black; the lowest-income owners skew old (`r p_fmt(pr("Householder age", "65 and over", ami_b1, "Owner"))` are 65 or over).

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Full detail: [Profiles](profiles.qmd). These figures come from household-level survey data (PUMS) for Richmond city, Henrico, and Chesterfield only, not the 17 localities used elsewhere on this page.
:::

## What to watch

::: callout-warning
## Seven things to look out for

1. **Growth leans on migration.** With natural increase down to `r n_fmt(per_year("rr17", era2, natural_change))` a year, a slowdown in international or domestic moves would show up directly in population growth. International migration in `r intl_last$year` was `r p_fmt(intl_last$international_mig / intl_peak$international_mig, 1)` of its `r intl_peak$year` peak.
2. **Home values are outrunning incomes.** Real home values rose `r p_fmt(real_chg(market$median_value, "40060"))` against `r p_fmt(inc_real_growth("40060"))` for income, and the value-to-income ratio widened from `r sprintf("%.1f", pti("40060", first_yr))` to `r sprintf("%.1f", pti("40060", latest_yr))`. The value measure is every owner's own estimate, so it understates the cost of buying today.
3. **Half of renters are cost-burdened, and the gap by income is wide.** The share did not improve over the decade, and the typical renter household earns far less than the typical owner household.
4. **Production is volatile and its mix keeps changing.** Permits swing between single-family and multifamily from year to year, and the expansion ring continues to build almost entirely detached homes (`r p_fmt(struct_share("secondary4", "Single-family detached"), 1)` of its stock) even though `r p_fmt(hh_share("rr17", "Living alone"), 1)` of the region's households are one person.
5. **Lower-income renters are where the burden concentrates.** Renters at 30% of AMI or less number `r n_fmt(P$band_counts |> filter(unit == "Households", ami5 == ami_b1, tenure == "Renter") |> pull(est))` households in the core three, and `r p_fmt(pbsev(ami_b1, "Renter"))` of them pay half or more of income on housing.
6. **The outer suburbs are the oldest part of the region.** The expansion ring has the highest 65-and-over share (`r p_fmt(age_share("secondary4", "65 and over"))`) and, in aggregate, more deaths than births in `r era2` (`r n_fmt(era_at("secondary4", era2, natural_change))`), so its growth depends entirely on in-migration.
7. **Access to credit is uneven, and eviction filings are back near their old level.** Black applicants were denied home-purchase loans `r sprintf("%.1f", hm_race("Black") / hm_race("White, non-Hispanic"))` times as often as non-Hispanic White applicants, and eviction filings in the latest 12 months were at `r round(ev_sum("bhc3", "latest12_pct_hist"))`% of the historical average, after a trough of `r n_fmt(ev_trough$filings)` filings in `r ev_trough$year`.
:::

## For external affairs: connecting the data to Better Housing Coalition's work

Better Housing Coalition (BHC) is the Richmond region's largest nonprofit affordable housing developer and property manager. It provides affordable rental housing and homeownership, operates 8 senior affordable properties, and is working to do more mixed-income, mixed-use development. The figures below are regional public data; each bullet names the part of BHC's work it speaks to.

### Quotable numbers

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bhc-numbers

bhc_tbl <- tribble(
  ~Figure, ~Value, ~`Margin of error (90%)`, ~Geography, ~Page, ~Caution,
  "Households at or below 80% of AMI",
    p_fmt(le80("All households")), au("le80_all"), "Core three", "Profiles", "",
  "Renter households at or below 80% of AMI",
    paste0(round_to(renters_le80), " (", p_fmt(le80("Renter")), " of renters)"), au("renters_le80"), "Core three", "Profiles", "Quote as \"about\"",
  "Renters at or below 30% of AMI paying half or more of income on housing",
    p_fmt(pbsev(ami_b1, "Renter")), au("renter_le30_sev"), "Core three", "Profiles", "",
  "Renter households paying 30%+ of income on housing",
    p_fmt(b30("rr17", "Renter")), au("renter_b30_2024"), "17-locality region", "Market", "",
  "Renter households at or below 50% of AMI with a householder 65 or over",
    paste0(round_to(senior_renters_le50, 500), " (", p_fmt(sr_share_le50, 1), ")"), au("senior_renters_le50"), "Core three", "Profiles",
    "Derived from a small sample (about 50 households); quote as \"about\"",
  "Population 65 and over",
    paste0(p_fmt(age_share("rr17", "65 and over", first_yr)), " to ", p_fmt(age_share("rr17", "65 and over"))), au("pop65_2024"), "17-locality region", "Demographics", "",
  "Median home value to median household income",
    paste0(sprintf("%.1f", pti("40060", first_yr)), " to ", sprintf("%.1f", pti("40060", latest_yr))), au("pti_2024"), "Richmond MSA", "Market", "",
  "Black vs. White non-Hispanic home-purchase denial rate",
    paste0(p_fmt(hm_race("Black")), " vs. ", p_fmt(hm_race("White, non-Hispanic"))),
    paste0(au("denial_Black"), " / ", au("denial_White")), "Core three", "Market",
    paste0("Loan records, not a sample; the interval shows only case-count noise. About ", p_fmt(au("hmda_unknown_race", "est"), 1), " of applications have no race/ethnicity"),
  "Eviction filings, latest 12 months vs. historical average",
    paste0(round(ev_sum("bhc3", "latest12_pct_hist")), "%"), au("evict_pct_hist"), "Core three", "Market",

)

bhc_tbl |>
  kbl(
    align = "lllllll",
    caption = paste0(
      "Figures for external communications, with margins of error. AMI = area median income. ACS and PUMS figures use the ",
      latest_yr, " 5-year window (changes are ", first_yr, " to ", latest_yr, "); the margin shown is for the latest figure. ",
      "Lending is ", (hm_last - 3), "-", hm_last, "; evictions run through ", format(evict$last_month, "%B %Y"), ". ",
      "Margins of error are published ACS values or PUMS replicate-weight standard errors x 1.645; see r/summary_audit.R."
    )
  ) |>
  kable_styling(c("condensed", "striped"))
```

### Affordable rental housing

- The core three have about `r round_to(renters_le80)` renter households at or below 80% of AMI, the income range where affordable rental housing is aimed. That is `r p_fmt(le80("Renter"))` of all renters, against `r p_fmt(le80("Owner"))` of owners.
- Need is deepest at the bottom: `r p_fmt(pbsev(ami_b1, "Renter"))` of renters at or below 30% of AMI pay half or more of their income on housing, and `r p_fmt(pb30(ami_b3, "Renter"))` of renters at 51-80% of AMI pay 30% or more. Above 120% of AMI, about `r p_fmt(pb30(ami_b5, "Renter"), 1)` do (a small sample, so quote it loosely).
- The burden is not easing region-wide: `r p_fmt(b30("rr17", "Renter"))` of renter households pay 30% or more (`r p_fmt(b30("rr17", "Renter", first_yr))` in `r first_yr`), and real median rent rose `r p_fmt(real_chg(market$median_rent, "40060"))` (`r au("rent_real_chg")`) while real median income rose `r p_fmt(inc_real_growth("40060"))` (`r au("income_real_chg")`); those two changes are within each other's margins of error, so do not say rent grew faster than income.
- Housing stability is part of the case: filings in the core three are back to `r round(ev_sum("bhc3", "latest12_pct_hist"))`% of the historical average, about `r round_to(ev_sum("bhc3", "latest12_mean"), 100)` a month, after falling to `r n_fmt(ev_trough$filings)` for all of `r ev_trough$year`. Filings are court requests, not completed evictions.
- Where the need is: `r p_fmt(1 - low_renter_city)` of the core three's lower-income renter households live in Henrico or Chesterfield, not Richmond city, even though the city has the highest share of lower-income households (`r p_fmt(le80("All households", "Richmond city"))`).

### Senior affordable housing

- The region's 65-and-over population grew from `r p_fmt(age_share("rr17", "65 and over", first_yr))` to `r p_fmt(age_share("rr17", "65 and over"))` of residents between the `r first_yr` and `r latest_yr` windows, so the group BHC's 8 senior properties serve is growing as a share of the region.
- About `r round_to(senior_renters_le50, 500)` renter households in the core three have a householder 65 or over and income at or below 50% of AMI, `r p_fmt(sr_share_le50, 1)` of all renter households in that range.
- Older owners are exposed too: `r p_fmt(pr("Householder age", "65 and over", ami_b1, "Owner"))` of owner households at or below 30% of AMI have a householder 65 or over, roughly `r round_to(senior_owners_le50, 500)` older owner households at or below 50% of AMI.
- The outer suburbs are the oldest part of the region (`r p_fmt(age_share("secondary4", "65 and over"))` aged 65 and over in the expansion ring), with more deaths than births in `r era2`, which points to a long-run need for senior housing outside the core.

### Homeownership

- The typical home was worth `r sprintf("%.1f", pti("40060", first_yr))` times the typical household income in the `r first_yr` window and `r sprintf("%.1f", pti("40060", latest_yr))` times in `r latest_yr`; real median home value rose `r p_fmt(real_chg(market$median_value, "40060"))` against `r p_fmt(inc_real_growth("40060"))` for income.
- About `r round_to(owners_le80)` owner households in the core three earn 80% of AMI or less (`r p_fmt(le80("Owner"))` of owners), and `r p_fmt(under50("rr17", "Renter"))` of renter households region-wide earn under $50,000, against `r p_fmt(under50("rr17", "Owner"))` of owners. The gap between the two groups is the gap affordable homeownership has to bridge.
- Access to credit is uneven: over `r (hm_last - 3)`-`r hm_last`, Black applicants were denied home-purchase loans `r p_fmt(hm_race("Black"))` of the time and Hispanic or Latino applicants `r p_fmt(hm_race("Hispanic or Latino"))`, against `r p_fmt(hm_race("White, non-Hispanic"))` for non-Hispanic White applicants.
- Across all denied applications (all loan purposes, `r min(hmda$reason_years)`-`r max(hmda$reason_years)`; most denials in the lending data are refinance, cash-out, and home-improvement loans, so do not describe these as home-purchase denial reasons), debt-to-income (`r p_fmt(hm_reason("Debt-to-income ratio"))`) and credit history (`r p_fmt(hm_reason("Credit history"))`) lead, ahead of collateral and cash to close.
- Lenders originated `r n_fmt(hm("bhc3", hm_last, "originated"))` home-purchase loans for principal residences in the core three in `r hm_last`, `r p_fmt(1 - hm("bhc3", hm_last, "originated") / hm("bhc3", hm_peak$activity_year, "originated"), 1)` below the `r hm_peak$activity_year` peak of `r n_fmt(hm("bhc3", hm_peak$activity_year, "originated"))`.

### Mixed-income, mixed-use development

- Richmond city is the one core locality where renters outnumber owners (`r n_fmt(hh("51760", "Renter"))` renter households to `r n_fmt(hh("51760", "Owner"))`) and the only one that is substantially multifamily, with `r p_fmt(struct_share("51760", "20+ units"), 1)` of units in buildings of 20 or more.
- The suburbs are built almost entirely as detached homes: `r p_fmt(struct_share("bhc3", "Single-family detached"), 1)` of the core's stock and `r p_fmt(struct_share("secondary4", "Single-family detached"), 1)` of the expansion ring's, even though `r p_fmt(hh_share("rr17", "Living alone"), 1)` of the region's households are one person.
- Production leans on multifamily in recent years: it outnumbered single-family permits in `r n_mf_lead` of the last 4 years and was `r p_fmt(perm_last$mf_share, 1)` of `r latest_bps` permitted units. Permits swing between `r n_fmt(perm_trough$total_units)` (`r perm_trough$year`) and `r n_fmt(perm_peak$total_units)` (`r perm_peak$year`) units a year.
- Lower-income households are spread across the core, not concentrated in one place: `r p_fmt(le80("All households", "Richmond city"))` of households in Richmond city, `r p_fmt(le80("All households", "Henrico County"))` in Henrico, and `r p_fmt(le80("All households", "Chesterfield County"))` in Chesterfield are at or below 80% of AMI. That supports mixed-income communities in all three localities, not only in the city.
- The region's housing stock is old in the city (`r p_fmt(prewar("51760"), 1)` of Richmond city's housing predates 1950) and tight in the suburbs (`r p_fmt(vac("51041"))` vacancy in Chesterfield), which limits the supply of affordable options without new construction.

::: callout-warning
## Using these figures in communications

- **These are regional figures, not BHC results.** They describe need and market conditions across Richmond city, Henrico, and Chesterfield (or the 17-locality region where noted). They do not count BHC's residents, properties, or outcomes; pair them with BHC's own program data.
- **Say "at or below 80% of AMI," not "low-income," without a definition.** AMI bands here follow HUD income limits for the Richmond area; see [Profiles](profiles.qmd).
- **PUMS counts are survey estimates.** Household counts by income band carry sampling error, so quote them rounded (for example, "about `r round_to(hh_count(ami_b1, "Renter"))` renter households at or below 30% of AMI").
- **Senior counts are derived and rest on a small sample.** They multiply the income-band count by the share of those households with a householder 65 or over (about 50 sample households for renters at or below 50% of AMI, margin of error `r au("senior_renters_le50")`), so quote them as "about" and round to the nearest 500.
- **Lending rates are not sampled, but have caveats.** HMDA counts reporting lenders' applications, so the margin shown is only case-count noise. Denial rates exclude withdrawn and incomplete applications; about `r p_fmt(au("hmda_unknown_race", "est"), 1)` of decided applications have no race or ethnicity recorded; lenders under the reporting threshold are not in the data.
- **The eviction baseline is the provider's.** The "percent of the historical average" has no documented definition. Prefer the count-based comparison (`r p_fmt(-ev_sum("bhc3", "latest12_vs_pre"), 1)` below the 2016-19 monthly mean) for anything external.
- **Check the wording of changes.** Home values rose far faster than incomes (outside the margins of error); rent and income changes are statistically similar.
- **The data do not measure demand for mixed-use space.** The mixed-income points rest on income, tenure, and structure-type patterns; retail and commercial demand needs separate evidence.
- **Eviction filings are not evictions.** Lead with the trend against the pre-2020 baseline, not a count of displaced households.
:::

::: callout-note
## Reading the numbers

- **Stock and production are different series.** Stock (ACS) counts units standing; production (Building Permits Survey) counts permits issued, which lead completions and can be cancelled.
- **Small geographies are noisy.** The four expansion-ring localities and Ashland carry wide margins of error; the pages suppress cells with a coefficient of variation above 30.
- **Income-band figures use a different geography.** They come from PUMS, which reports only whole PUMAs; the seven used here tile Richmond city, Henrico, and Chesterfield exactly. The other localities are not covered, so these totals will not match the 17-locality pages.
- **Eviction and lending figures cover the core three only.** Eviction filings are court records and lending figures are HMDA loan-level data; neither is ACS, so they will not reconcile with the 17-locality pages. Denial rates count denied / (originated + approved-not-accepted + denied) and are shown only where at least 100 applications were decided.
- **Migration figures are modeled** from administrative records and revised each vintage. The 2010-2019 and 2020-2025 series come from different vintages and are compared, not joined.
- **Dollar changes are inflation-adjusted** with national CPI-U, so they measure change relative to national prices, not a local cost-of-living index.
- See [Data Notes](data-notes.qmd) for sources and definitions.
:::
